terms.definition: Compaction that replaces old content with content-addressed stubs the agent can fetch on demand, instead of a paraphrase. Lossless by construction.
terms.note: Measured at +19.43 points over the best lossy baseline on a 1,000-task needle benchmark [S].

terms.definition: A short, numbered Markdown record of a design decision, committed to the repository and reviewed in the pull request that makes the decision.
terms.note: The best memory for coding agents in this research: versioned, greppable and repaired by the same process that changes the code.

terms.definition: A retrieval control strategy where the agent iterates: search, read, decide the next query, stop when satisfied.
terms.note: The dominant architecture in shipped coding agents, and the axis where harness differences bite hardest.

terms.definition: The framing that replaces "context window as container": adding tokens can redistribute useful signal rather than creating more reliable attention.
The one limitation that currently caps your agent's results. Fixing anything else changes little until it moves.
Segments 5–9 of the context: retrieved code, tool results, agent messages, user turns and summaries. It grows during a session.
terms.note: Appended content may be reusable once unchanged; cache hits and billing depend on the provider and request construction. Contrast with the prefix.

terms.definition: Input cost with cached and uncached tokens priced separately, about 0.10 versus 1.25 in relative units.
terms.note: The only honest cost metric, because context changes often move the ratio rather than the total.

terms.definition: A failure mode where the context contains contradictions from different phases and the model resolves them by recency or by blending.
The import, call, reference and type graph of a codebase, computed exactly by a compiler or language server.
terms.note: Free, always current, and the basis of structural retrieval. Not the same thing as a knowledge graph.

terms.definition: Replacing part of a transcript with a summary. Irreversible, within one session, and it invalidates the cache from the point of change.
terms.note: Distinct from offload (reversible) and memory (across sessions).

terms.definition: The property that makes delegation safe: sub-agent outputs combine without negotiation.
terms.note: Search and survey work is composable. Interlocking implementation is not.

terms.definition: A failure mode where irrelevant context is used because it is present. The common case is picking a plausible wrong tool when too many are in scope.
The everyday name for performance becoming less reliable as input length grows. Chroma measured the pattern across 18 models, with non-uniform curves that depend on model and task [S].
A sub-agent knew something relevant but did not report it because its output contract did not ask.
terms.note: The parent cannot recover it unless the sub-agent's transcript was saved.

terms.definition: The policy for external prose such as a wiki: fetch a named page on demand, never bulk-ingest it into a retrieval store.
A failure mode where the agent imitates its own transcript instead of reasoning: re-running, re-reading, re-proposing.
The length at which a model still performs acceptably on a given task, as opposed to the length it advertises; it may be shorter than the advertised maximum.
A tag on a claim saying how it is supported: S (sourced), P (practitioner-reported), D (derived) or C (composite).
Reasoning about a code fragment without the control flow around it, such as a grep hit shown without the if statement that governs it.
The software wrapping the model: system prompt, tools, loop, compaction and retrieval behaviour.
terms.note: Harness effects can exceed the effect of the strategy under test, so results rarely transfer between harnesses [S].

terms.definition: Splitting context across boundaries such as sub-agents or sessions. It shrinks the parent's context at the expense of total spend.
Carrying lightweight identifiers such as paths and symbol names, and fetching content only at the moment it is needed.
Entities and relations extracted from prose by an LLM pipeline. Approximate and as stale as its last ingestion.
terms.note: Skipped for coding work: over source code the code graph answers the same questions exactly. Useful for cross-system relationships.

terms.definition: Compaction turning a hedged hypothesis into an asserted fact by stripping the uncertainty around it.
A check that flags the same tool called with the same arguments three or more times with no new information in between.
terms.note: The cheapest high-signal instrument available, and rarely built.

terms.definition: Replacing old tool output with placeholders. Needs no model call.
terms.note: Matched LLM summarisation on solve rate at lower cost [S], so it is the baseline any summariser must beat.

terms.definition: The Model Context Protocol: a standard way to expose tools and data to agents through servers.
terms.note: The protocol is fine. Attaching many servers by default is the problem.

terms.definition: Information persisted across sessions. Justified only by retrievals that changed an action, not by what was written.
Moving content out of the window into addressable storage and leaving a stub the agent can follow back. Reversible.
Pass@k counts a task solved if any of k runs succeed ("can it ever?"). Pass^k, written Pass² for k = 2, requires all k runs to succeed ("can it reliably?").
terms.note: Compression damages Pass^k far more than Pass@k, which is why single runs miss it.

terms.definition: A failure mode where a false fact enters the context and is afterwards treated as established. It survives compaction and cannot be removed by appending a correction.
A critical fact becoming harder to use because its position in a long input is less favourable.
terms.note: The size and shape of the effect depend on the model, task and harness [S].

terms.definition: Segments 1–4 of the context: system prompt, tool definitions, instruction files and skill descriptions. Usually stable and sent on each call; it may be reusable when unchanged, while billing depends on cached versus uncached rates.
Reusing the computed state of an unchanged prompt prefix. Prefix-exact: valid up to the first changed byte.
The tokens present in segments 1–4 on each call before any work. Measure them by sending a one-token message in a fresh session; billing depends on cache hits.
Loading short descriptions first and full content only on demand. Applied to tool schemas, skills and file reads.
terms.note: About 25,000 tokens of tool definitions became about 2,500 tokens of descriptions [S].

terms.definition: Whether the decisive file was ever opened during a failed task. It separates starvation from dilution, which need opposite fixes.
The share of retrieved tokens that appear in the final change or explanation. Low values mean retrieval is wasteful.
Tokens that could plausibly be cited in a correct answer, divided by all tokens in context. The working measure of dilution.
Ending a session and starting a fresh one seeded with a plan file or handoff note. The only operation that removes poisoned content.
The sum of each segment's tokens multiplied by the number of turns it stays in context. The true cost of hoarding.
Compacting on task events such as a sub-goal closing or a test passing, instead of at a token threshold or on a timer.
A named capability with a short trigger description that is always loaded and a full procedure that loads only when it matches.
How fast a fact stops being true. Where a fact should live depends on whether the store's repair rate beats it.
The agent lacks a fact, does not know it is missing, and proceeds on an assumption. A clean trajectory and a wrong answer.
terms.note: The fifth failure mode this research adds. It can survive review because the transcript may look clean.

terms.definition: Retrieving code by symbol, reference and import graph instead of by whole file or embedding similarity.
What stays in context after an offload: an identifier plus just enough description to decide whether to fetch it.
terms.note: A bare identifier is dead weight; a pointer the agent will not follow is equivalent to deletion.

terms.definition: A separate agent with its own fresh context, given a bounded task and returning a result to a parent agent.
Tool definitions taking a large share of the prefix. Harms through displacement and through selection confusion.
A confidence interval for a success rate that behaves well at small sample sizes.
